title: Working for Benny Goodman: how it started and the Goodman Story near miss
summary: Goodman liked him on a Basie broadcast, he first worked with Goodman's big band in the mid-1950s, and nearly appeared in the Benny Goodman Story.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Well, actually, I worked with Benny -- it really started around -- in the early '50s. Maybe -- you know, I could have joined Benny's band when I was with Basie's band. I started to. Later then, after Cootie {Williams} had joined the band, he asked me if I wanted to join the band. And maybe through John, John might have -- but he always dug me, you know, because I remember one time, I told Benny this, too, we broadcast from the Hotel Sherman. I think it was the Panther Room. and Benny heard the broadcast. He said, "Oh, that new tenor player," he says, "man, I like that new tenor player." And he told Basie. So Basie said Benny said, "That's it," said, "you the tenor player. So that seals that."
So when I told Benny, Benny said, "Well, hell, you wasn't working for me, you was working for him." I said, "But you said I was a good tenor player." He said, "That's it."
Well, actually, I don't know, my first engagement with him, it must have been with a big band. Maybe around '55 or '56 or something. I almost got in the Benny Goodman Story.
You know? I was surprised he didn't have
Vido. But I think they fell out. They had a falling out somewhere. But he had Stan and I almost was in that. Buck was in it.

Uh-huh. And I had a gig -- I think I would have been -- I probably wouldn't have got a chance to play a solo or anything, but I would have at least been in the band. But I had to go away somewhere, I don't remember, but I couldn't get it. But everytime he had a chance, he'd always call me and get me a gig.
